Albina is located in eastern Suriname on the Marowijne River. Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni in French Guiana lies on the opposite bank. Albina is therefore associated with river crossings and travel between two countries. The river both shapes the town's landscape and marks the international border.

Travelers cross the river from Albina in small boats and continue their journey on the French side. Exploring the town reveals the geography of the Guianas through travel on the water and the closeness of the neighboring riverbanks. Albina adds a distinct riverside stop to routes from Paramaribo to French Guiana and forms part of this region of South America.

Almirante is an important mainland connection on routes to Bocas del Toro. Here, the road gives way to a boat crossing to Colón Island. The piers and movement of boats offer a glimpse of everyday life on Panama's Caribbean coast.

A stop in Almirante lets you experience the link between the mainland and the island archipelago. The journey then continues amid the seascapes of Bocas del Toro. The town itself is an interesting coastal gateway to the islands, with small boats, waterfront buildings and views over the water.

Ambergris Caye, an island fringed by palm trees, lies 58 km north of Belize City. The island stretches for 40 kilometers, yet is only 1,600 meters wide. You can easily walk from one coast to the other. Colorful sandy beaches, lagoons, mangrove thickets, tropical savanna and turquoise coastal waters all lie beneath the hot sun. The coastal waters are considered an excellent place for diving. Here you can enjoy drift diving, swimming with the currents, windsurfing, snorkeling, sea fishing and sailing. The water is so clear, with visibility of up to 60 meters, that you can observe the diversity of underwater life even without diving.

Travelers interested in the ancient past can discover Mayan architectural remains and limestone caves on Ambergris Caye, where members of the ancient civilization held rituals. Archaeological work here has uncovered remarkable artifacts. Enjoy the natural surroundings and white sandy beaches, look around and listen to the songs of the island's birds, said to be unlike those on the mainland; more than 200 varieties are found here.

The island's greatest tourist attraction is the magnificent Barrier Reef, which runs parallel to the coastline. The reef lies just a quarter of a mile from the beach, making it readily accessible for snorkeling and scuba diving.

The Great Blue Hole and Hol Chan Marine Reserve are must-see attractions on an Ambergris Caye itinerary. The Blue Hole is a circular limestone sinkhole reaching a depth of 122 meters. Here, you can dive into deep ultramarine waters and encounter various sharks, hammerhead sharks and colorful reef fish. In Hol Chan, where depths reach only 30 meters, there are more than 150 species of exotic fish and 40 varieties of coral, along with sea turtles and sharks.
